findings.explanation: By default, SC4SNMP writes polled numeric values to the metrics index `netmetrics` with sourcetype `sc4snmp:metric`, and non-metric values to `netops` with `sc4snmp:event`. It never writes `snmp:apc:cooling` into `index=cooling`, so a reader who picks SC4SNMP gets zero results from this SPL. There is also no MIB module called 'AirIR-MIB'. The InRow objects sit in the airIR subtree of PowerNet-MIB, and an SC4SNMP profile that names 'AirIR-MIB' will not resolve.
findings.quote: Splunk Connect for SNMP (SC4SNMP) or SNMP Modular Input; APC PowerNet-MIB / AirIR-MIB field extractions
findings.suggested_fix: Name one collector. For SC4SNMP, say the data arrives as metrics such as `sc4snmp.PowerNet-MIB.airIRRCUnitStatusFanSpeed` in the configured metrics index and needs `mstats`, or describe the custom sourcetype override. For the SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase 1537), describe the stanza that sets `sourcetype=snmp:apc:cooling`. Replace 'AirIR-MIB' with 'PowerNet-MIB (airIR / airIRRC subtree)'.

findings.explanation: The Universal Forwarder is downloaded from splunk.com, not Splunkbase, and it has no SNMP modular input of its own. Splunkbase /app/617 returns 404. The sentence tells the reader to install a non-existent app as the SNMP collector.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 'Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)'. Say the data comes from SC4SNMP or from the SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase 1537) running on a heavy forwarder, and match the index to the SPL (`index=cooling`) rather than `index=power|cooling|environment`.

findings.explanation: The `implementation` field describes a load-normalised alert (+20 points at the same load) and a per-season baseline. The `spl` field is only a 24-hour `timechart` of avg fan % and airflow: it reads no load or cooling-demand value, stores no baseline and has no threshold. So `detailedImplementation`'s 'throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages' has nothing to page on.
findings.quote: (2) Alert when fan_pct rises 20 points at same load.
findings.suggested_fix: Either describe this as a trending dashboard with no alert, or say how load is measured (for example `airIRRCUnitStatusCoolDemand` / `airIRRCUnitStatusCoolOutput`), where the seasonal baseline is stored (lookup or summary index) and the exact comparison that raises an alert.

findings.explanation: The steps are a generic REST-API template: vendor API rate limits, the HTTP 401/429 'vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf', a 'vendor admin UI inventory count' and a placeholder `tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...`. None of it covers SNMP polling of an InRow NMC: SNMP community or v3 credentials, the OIDs to poll, mapping `airIRRCUnitIdentName` to `unit_name`, or the tenths-of-percent scaling.
findings.quote: Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=snmp:apc:cooling into cooling. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs`
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the steps for SNMP. Enable SNMP on the InRow network management card. Poll `airIRRCUnitStatusFanSpeed` (tenths of percent), `airIRRCUnitStatusAirFlowUS` (CFM) and `airIRRCUnitIdentName`. Extract or rename them to the SPL fields and validate against the unit's front-panel or web UI readings.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified even though its MIB object names do not exist in PowerNet-MIB, it cites a non-existent Splunkbase app, and its text is template residue. That is not consistent with SME sign-off.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the status to a draft or unverified value until an SME has checked the collector, OIDs and field mapping against a real InRow unit.

findings.explanation: The Schneider reference is a PDU product-category page, not InRow cooling, and the Splunkbase link is a search URL. Nothing points to the PowerNet-MIB objects the UC depends on.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the InRow RC/RP SNMP or PowerNet-MIB documentation, the SNMP Modular Input page (https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1537) or the SC4SNMP docs.

findings.explanation: The UC trends polled gauge values, and no trap feeds this search.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `snmp_trap` unless a trap-based step is added.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `airIRFanSpeed` and `airIRFanAirflow` are not PowerNet-MIB objects. The InRow RC objects are `airIRRCUnitStatusFanSpeed`, which is in tenths of percent and must be divided by 10 to give fan_pct, and `airIRRCUnitStatusAirFlowUS` (CFM) or `airIRRCUnitStatusAirFlowMetric` (hundredths of L/s). InRow RP units use the airIRRP100/airIRRP500 prefixes. With SC4SNMP the values are metrics and need `mstats` against the metrics index. Evidence: https://oidref.com/1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.13.3.2.2.2

summary: The UC aims at a real signal: InRow fan speed and airflow trends. The collection text is wrong, though. SC4SNMP does not emit `snmp:apc:cooling` events, 'AirIR-MIB' is not a MIB, and the Universal Forwarder is not Splunkbase app 617. The SPL reads MIB object names that do not exist, the implementation promises a load-normalised alert the SPL never computes, and the rest is generic template text.
